title: Derived dual of the completed residue coefficient sheaf
statement: Let ell be prime, E a finite extension of Q_ell and X a scheme. Use the small completed coefficient ring and positive-level-one residue sheaf Q=SmallAdicCompletion.finiteModule ell E X 0 of [det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model]. In the ordinary relative derived category of completed coefficient module sheaves, RHom(Q[0],1) is isomorphic to Q[0][-1]. Thus the residue sheaf in degree zero has its dual in degree one.

source.place: Proof, final two sentences: the residue example (step 10)

proof.text: The coefficient DVR theorem gives a nonzero uniformizer pi generating a nonzero maximal ideal. Its principal ideal is open: the norm ball of radius |pi| lies in it, since x/pi is integral whenever |x|≤|pi|. Hence O/(pi) is discrete. On every profinite U the quotient C(U,O)→C(U,O/(pi)) is surjective by choosing representatives in the discrete quotient and composing with a continuous function. Its kernel consists of pi multiples: division by the nonzero constant pi is continuous, takes integral values on the kernel, and gives the preimage. Multiplication by pi is injective pointwise. Forgetting module actions, sheafification of this sectionwise short exact sequence gives a short exact sequence of regular condensed modules with residue quotient. Exact pullback from the point gives 0→1→1→Q→0 on X.

source.place: Proof, residue example and its uniformizer resolution; Stacks 0FPU

proof.text: In any braided closed derived category, for f:1→1 one has id_1 followed by pre(f) = f followed by id_1, proved by uncurrying and unitor naturality. Apply derived internal Hom into 1 to the distinguished triangle 1→1→Q→1[1]. The dual triangle, rotated once, begins with pre(f), which is identified with f by the canonical isomorphism 1≅RHom(1,1). The isomorphism of the first two entries extends to an isomorphism of distinguished triangles. Its third component identifies Q with RHom(Q,1)[1]; shifting back yields RHom(Q,1)≅Q[-1]. Apply this to the single-complex triangle of the short exact sequence. The shift -1 places the cokernel in cohomological degree 1.

theorem integralHeart_residue_dual
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : Type v) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic ℓ) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic ℓ) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    Nonempty
      ((((CondensedRing.derivedHom (SmallAdicCompletion.Coefficients.integerRing ℓ E)
          X).obj (op ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
            (SmallAdicCompletion.finiteModule ℓ E X 0)))).obj
              (𝟙_ (integralHeartDerivedCategory.{u} ℓ E X))) ≅
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          (SmallAdicCompletion.finiteModule ℓ E X 0))⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧)
